findings.passage: Under both existing law and Senate Bill 1174, all local governments — including charter cities like Huntington Beach — are prohibited from disenfranchising voters at the polls by implementing voter ID requirements. Let me be clear: that has not changed. We disagree with the court’s decision that it is too early to bring our lawsuit, and remain confident in the strength of our case.
findings.note: Attorney General press release on a court ruling in the state's suit against Huntington Beach's voter ID measure; he cites existing law and SB 1174 on local voter ID rules.

findings.passage: Today’s victory makes one thing crystal clear: No city in our state, charter and non-charter alike, is above the law. All along, Secretary of State Weber and I have maintained that Huntington Beach’s voter ID policy is illegal, and now, the state’s highest court has weighed in and agreed with us. Measure A won’t be taking effect — ever,
findings.note: Attorney General release after the California Supreme Court declined to review the ruling that blocked Huntington Beach's voter ID requirement.

findings.passage: Huntington Beach’s leaders have been parroting the Trump Administration’s talking points by questioning the integrity of our elections. In court, the City’s allegations were resoundingly rejected. I remain fully committed to protecting the right to vote from baseless attacks.
findings.note: Same release; he addresses claims about election integrity that the city made in the case.

findings.passage: My fellow attorneys general and I are taking him to court because this Executive Order is nothing but a blatantly illegal power grab and an attempt to disenfranchise voters. Neither the Constitution nor Congress authorize the President’s attempted voting restrictions.
findings.note: Release announcing a multistate suit over the 2025 federal elections executive order, which includes documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration.

findings.passage: This order is just as illegal as the first one. But the president seems to embrace a philosophy of if at first you don't succeed, break the law again.
findings.note: Quoted by ABC7 San Francisco when he filed a suit over the 2026 executive order on mail-in voting and citizenship verification (filed on a Friday in early April 2026, per the report).

findings.motion: State of California v. City of Huntington Beach, suit against Measure A voter ID requirement, filed April 2024, ended after the California Supreme Court declined review
findings.note: As Attorney General he brought, with the Secretary of State, the suit that blocked a city's local voter ID rule. The release says the suit was filed in April 2024.

findings.motion: Co-led multistate lawsuit against the 2025 federal elections executive order (documentary proof of citizenship and related provisions)
findings.note: He co-led a coalition of state attorneys general suing over an executive order that would require documentary proof of citizenship to register in federal elections.
